core.title: Derive contract layout (FLAT, FACETED, COLLECTION) from the artifact name
core.given: An artifact named {domain}:{resource}[.{category}] (colon = hierarchy, dot = facet; optional category for nested resources) is declared, or its contract schemas/tests are placed, moved or corrected
core.when: the planner chooses or states its contract layout within the contract tree (schema and test locations per the profile: layout.contract_paths#contract_flat, layout.contract_paths#contract_faceted, layout.contract_paths#contract_collection)
core.then: Determine the layout in order: (1) a dot facet in the name → FACETED, schema at layout.contract_paths#contract_faceted; (2) a resource holding multiple schema files → COLLECTION, schemas at layout.contract_paths#contract_collection; (3) otherwise → FLAT, schema at layout.contract_paths#contract_flat.
prefer: FLAT (single schema, single resource): schema at layout.contract_paths#contract_flat; schema tests at the FLAT test location (layout.contract_paths#contract_tests).
FACETED (category as dot facet): schema at layout.contract_paths#contract_faceted; schema tests at the FACETED test location (layout.contract_paths#contract_tests).

COLLECTION (one artifact, several related schemas in one directory): schemas at layout.contract_paths#contract_collection; schema tests at the COLLECTION test location (layout.contract_paths#contract_tests); optional master-index schema (layout.contract_paths#contract_catalog); each schema's metadata: collection: true, resource (same for all), member (identifies the schema).
Example comments cue noun number (plural → COLLECTION, singular → FLAT); the source gives no precedence over the order in then.

Unresolved source conflict: the source's dotted FLAT examples contradict 'dot → FACETED' with no stated criterion. Follow the order by default; if you depart, state the mapping in the plan and flag the ambiguity.

The source's generic physical pattern (layout.contract_paths#contract_generic) and the concrete layout patterns disagree on the schema file suffix; this discrepancy is unresolved — name the file suffix explicitly in the plan.
avoid: Over-nesting a single resource: storing a single-schema resource in its own resource directory instead of the flat schema location (layout.contract_paths#contract_flat).
Contract paths not derivable from the logical name (layout chosen ad hoc).
core.why: A deterministic name→layout mapping lets the path be derived from the logical name, keeps simple resources flat and supports faceted and multi-schema resources without ambiguity; domain-based organization gives clear ownership and REST API mapping.
evidence: Every artifact name resolves to one layout per the determination order (FACETED, COLLECTION or FLAT, at the profile's layout patterns). Where a path matches only a source example that conflicts with the order (a dotted name mapped FLAT, an example-only path prefix not derivable from {domain}, a generic-pattern vs concrete-layout file-suffix discrepancy), the outcome is 'unresolved conflict' for reviewer decision — neither auto-pass by example name nor auto-fail — and the plan must state the chosen mapping.
Schema tests sit in the test location matching the layout (per layout.contract_paths#contract_tests).
COLLECTION members carry metadata {collection: true, resource: <shared>, member: <specific>}; the optional master index (layout.contract_paths#contract_catalog) acts as the collection's index.
No single-schema resource is stored over-nested (a resource directory holding only the resource's own schema) instead of the flat location.
verification: Deterministic check: map each declared artifact name to its expected layout by the determination order — (1) dot facet → FACETED, (2) multiple schema files → COLLECTION, (3) otherwise FLAT — using the profile's layout patterns, and compare with the actual contract tree.

Strict disposition on source conflicts: any path matching only a source example that conflicts with the determination order — a dotted name mapped FLAT, a path prefix that appears only in examples and is not derivable from {domain}, or a generic-pattern vs concrete-layout file-suffix discrepancy — is reported 'unresolved conflict' for reviewer decision; neither auto-pass by example-name match nor auto-fail; matching an example name alone is not a compliance criterion.
The generic-vs-concrete file-suffix discrepancy is reported unresolved, never silently normalised; the plan must state the schema file suffix explicitly.

Example-comment cues (plural noun → COLLECTION, singular noun → FLAT) carry no stated precedence over the determination order; the check does not treat them as rules and does not generalise example-only path prefixes into routing rules.
Collection check: member schemas carry the collection metadata; the master index is optional; schema tests sit in the layout-matching test location; no single-schema resource is stored over-nested.

Observability limits: file-kind matching relies on the profile's contract layout patterns (glob-matchable); detecting added/renamed artifact names and moved/renamed schema or schema-test files needs a diff-level observer; whether a planner is choosing a layout and whether a resource will hold several schemas needs semantic reading (llm-judged), not a mechanical check.

values: planner states or chooses a contract layout
resource will hold several related schemas

fires: A plan or wagon declares a new artifact {domain}:{resource} and names where its contract schema will live.
A planner introduces a dot-faceted artifact name {domain}:{resource}.{category} in a produce/consume list.
A planner specifies a resource that will hold several related schema files under one artifact name.
A plan proposes an over-nested single-schema layout (a resource directory holding only the resource's own schema) instead of the flat schema location.
A task relocates, renames or corrects the layout of existing contract schemas or schema tests (e.g. flattening an over-nested resource, converting between FACETED and COLLECTION).
A doc or acceptance describes the expected contract path for an existing artifact name.
doesNotFire: Editing fields inside an existing schema without changing the artifact name, its file location or its test location.
Work that neither names, places, moves nor corrects any contract artifact or schema file.
Code-layer file placement outside the contract tree (governed by other layout conventions).

neutralityNotes: The artifact logical-name grammar {domain}:{resource}[.{category}] (colon = hierarchy, dot = facet) and the collection metadata field names (collection, resource, member) stay in the core: they are methodology-level interface content, name no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, and are the rule's subject matter. Every concrete path, test-path pattern, the catalog file name and both sides of the .json vs .schema.json discrepancy moved to proposed layout.* profile keys, since the closed vocabulary has no contract-tree keys; instantiated with these values the core reproduces the Bun obligation exactly (no exception or condition dropped, none added). The 'unresolved conflict' disposition, the no-auto-pass-by-example-name rule and the no-generalisation rule for example-only prefixes are per-rule verification, not profile keys. Source examples — including the literal commons/ prefix, which the source gives no routing rule for — remain only in bun.json, the delivered reference example. The path_glob activation fact was converted to a file_kind fact because path_glob is outside the neutral fact vocabulary; its literal globs are realization data. 'REST API mapping' in why is the source's rationale and was kept.
